rag.description: Middle-clicks an element or the current pointer position, for example to open a link in a new tab. The element is located and brought into view before the click, a missing element fails the step, and the optional element target keeps scripted pointer workflows reliable.

qa.question: What does the InvokeMiddleClick action do?
qa.answer: It presses and releases the middle mouse button (the wheel button) on an element, or at the current pointer position when no element is given.

qa.question: Which inputs does InvokeMiddleClick use?
qa.answer: It takes no parameters; the optional OnElement and Locator properties choose the element to middle-click.

qa.question: Where does InvokeMiddleClick fit in an automation workflow?
qa.answer: It runs as a WebDriver task step labeled Invoke Middle Click; place it where a flow must open a link in a new tab, close a tab with a middle click, or trigger middle-button behavior.

qa.question: What is a good practice when using InvokeMiddleClick without an element?
qa.answer: Place a pointer move step such as MoveMouseCursor first, because without OnElement the click lands wherever the pointer already is.

qa.question: How is an InvokeMiddleClick rule defined?
qa.answer: Use $type Action with pluginName InvokeMiddleClick, and add onElement with a locator such as Xpath or CssSelector to target an element.

qa.question: What is the manifest version of InvokeMiddleClick?
How do the InvokeMiddleClick description and summary explain it?
qa.answer: They describe a middle-button click that opens links in new tabs and triggers wheel-button behavior on an element or at the current pointer position.

qa.question: What happens when the InvokeMiddleClick element cannot be found?
qa.answer: The step fails with an element lookup or timeout error and no click is sent. Documentation: https://github.com/g4-api/g4-plugins/blob/main/docs/Actions/InvokeMiddleClick.md Source: https://github.com/g4-api/g4-plugins/blob/main/src/G4.Plugins.Ui/Actions/InvokeMiddleClick.cs

description: ### Purpose
Performs a middle-click, a press and release of the middle mouse button, on an element or at the current pointer position.
When an element is given, the action brings it into view and moves the pointer to its center before clicking.
Use it to open a link in a new tab, close a tab, or trigger any behavior bound to the middle mouse button.
For left-clicks use InvokeClick, and for right-clicks use InvokeContextClick.
### Key Features and Functionality
| Feature             | Description                                                                     |
| Middle Click        | Presses and releases the middle mouse button through the WebDriver Actions API. |
| Auto Scroll         | Brings the element into view before the pointer moves to it.                    |
| Element Centering   | Moves the pointer to the center of the element, then clicks there.              |
| Positional Click    | Middle-clicks at the current pointer position when no element is given.         |
| Locator Flexibility | Finds the element with Xpath, CssSelector, Id, LinkText, or PartialLinkText.    |
### Usages in RPA
| Use Case                | Description                                                                         |
| Open Links in New Tabs  | Opens several result or report links in background tabs to process them one by one. |
| Close Browser Tabs      | Closes a tab by middle-clicking its tab header in applications that support it.     |
| Positional Middle Click | Middle-clicks at a position set by an earlier pointer move step.                    |
### Usages in Automation Testing
| Use Case               | Description                                                                    |
| New Tab Link Testing   | Verifies that middle-clicking a link opens it in a new tab and keeps the page. |
| Middle Button Handlers | Confirms that elements react correctly to middle-button events.                |
| Regression Testing     | Checks that middle-click behavior stays the same after application updates.    |

edge_cases: Element is covered by another element, so the middle-click may land on the covering element
Element is inside an iframe, so the driver must switch to that frame first
Page ignores middle-button events, so nothing visible happens
annotations.expected_result: The link matched by the CSS selector #ReportLink receives a middle-click and opens in a new browser tab.
annotations.notes: The element is brought into view and the pointer moves to its center before the middle button is pressed and released. CssSelector is used because onElement is a CSS selector.

description: ### Middle-click an element located by a CSS selector
Finds the element matching `#ReportLink` with the CssSelector strategy, moves the pointer to its center, and middle-clicks it.
On a link, the browser usually opens the target in a new tab.

edge_cases: Content moved after the pointer was positioned, so the click may hit a different element
Focus is on another window, so the click may not reach the intended page
No earlier pointer move happened, so the click lands at the default pointer position
annotations.expected_result: A middle-click is performed at the current pointer position without locating any element.
annotations.notes: Without onElement the middle button is pressed and released wherever the pointer already is. Place a pointer move step, such as MoveMouseCursor, before this step.

description: ### Middle-click at the current pointer position
Presses and releases the middle mouse button at the current pointer position without locating an element.
Use it after a step that already moved the pointer to the target.
Locator selects the strategy used to find the element named by OnElement.
Accepted values are Xpath, CssSelector, Id, LinkText, and PartialLinkText, and Xpath is used when it is absent.
Locator has an effect only when OnElement is also provided.
properties.name: Locator

description: OnElement holds the locator expression of the element to middle-click.
It is read with the strategy set by the Locator property.
When it is absent, the middle-click happens at the current pointer position instead.
properties.name: OnElement

summary: Middle-clicks an element or the current pointer position by pressing and releasing the middle mouse button.
Brings the element into view and clicks its center, so links open in a new tab and wheel-button handlers fire.
Helps RPA flows open links in background tabs and helps tests verify middle-click behavior.
